text:
Lamarre-Condon says friend cited Taylor Swift song No Body, No Crime and told him not to go to police
Two days after the alleged murders, Lamarre-Condon says he turned up in a van with the bodies in the back at the home of a friend, known to the court under the pseudonym Elizabeth Kennedy.
He warned her he was not joking and said she could be charged with being an accessory before showing her Baird’s head, the jury hears.
When Lamarre-Condon suggested he should go to the police, he tells the court she said “No, no, they might not believe you.”
He says Kennedy then referred to the Taylor Swift song No Body, No Crime.
She’s a big Taylor Swift fan.
She just wanted to be a good friend and help me. She thought I would actually get killed in jail.
Lamarre-Condon confirmed to the court he went to a sushi train the day after the alleged murders and discussed shooting Baird with his friend.
The friend previously gave evidence that Lamarre-Condon had confessed the crimes to him, forming his hand into a gun gesture and saying “pew pew”.
But asked if he had said this, Lamarre-Condon tells the jury:
I’ve never said ‘pew pew’ in my life . That’s something a kid would say.
I didn’t shoot the second person, I wanted to call police back but I couldn’t take the risk [they would think] I had shot a witness or this was a domestic.
Lamarre-Condon says he thought he would be ‘signing my own death wish’ if he went to police
The accused says he was “guilty of manslaughter” over the death of Jesse Baird and knew the maximum sentence was 25 years in prison and was worried about what would happen to him in jail.
In my mind I was fearful that if I went to police, if I did the right thing, I was signing my own death wish by potentially getting stabbed or killed in jail.
I genuinely believed if I was going to jail I would be killed.
Not because of who I was as a person, but because of the uniform I wear.
Lamarre-Condon tells court about buying second surfboard cover
The former police officer said he was intending to buy suitcases or a sleeping bag but decided to buy another surfboard cover after the alleged murders because he knew he already had one.
‘I killed somebody’: Lamarre-Condon told friend he shot Jesse Baird
Lamarre-Condon arrived at a friend’s work and told him about the shootings, the jury heard.
“I said ‘I killed somebody’, referring to a singular person and I continued the conversation with him.
“I said the first shot got Jesse … went through the shoulder and out the door and the second shot went through the door … I never said anything about shooting Luke ... I only told him about two shots going off related to Jesse Baird and Jesse Baird only.”
digest_he:
בו למאר-קונדון, שוטר לשעבר הנאשם ברצח כפול של זוגתו לשעבר ג'סי בירד ובן זוגו לוק דייוויס, המשיך במתן עדותו בבית המשפט וסיפר על הצעדים שננקטו לאחר האירועים.

לדבריו, הוא הגיע לביתה של ידידה יומיים לאחר הרצח כשהגופות ברכבו, ואף הציג לה את ראשו של בירד תוך אזהרה כי היא עלולה להיות מעורבת כשותפה לדבר עבירה. עוד טען כי חשש פן יחוסל בכלא בשל מדיו ולכן נמנע מלהסגיר את עצמו למשטרה, והודה כי הוא אשם בהריגה בלבד ולא ברצח מכוון.

במהלך העדות התייחס הנאשם לרכישת כיסוי לגלשן וטענות נוספות הקשורות למהלכיו בימים שקדמו לרצח ובמהלכו, כאשר המשפט בראשות השופטת נטלי אדמס נמשך.
